Aberration budget analysis of EUV lithography
from the imaging performance of a contact layer
in a 5 nm technology node

Zhishu Chen,1,2,* Lisong Dong,1,2,3,4 Huwen Ding,1,2  AND Yayi Wei1,2,3,5

1Institute of Microelectronics of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100029, China
2University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100049, China
3Guangdong Greater Bay Area Applied Research Institute of Integrated Circuit and Systems, Guangzhou 510700, China
4donglisong@ime.ac.cn

Received 25 May 2023; revised 31 August 2023; accepted 2 September 2023; posted 5 September 2023; published 15 September 2023


    By analyzing the impact of aberration in an extreme ultraviolet lithography projector on the imaging indicators
      of the test patterns for a contact layer in a 5 nm technology node, this paper establishes a mathematical aberration
     model based on the back propagating neutral network. On the basis of an aberration model, a method for esti-
     mating the aberration budget is proposed, which can help reduce the difﬁculty of achieving imaging performance
      thresholds in actual production. The performance of the results given by this method is veriﬁed by using a rigorous
      simulation. The results show that the model is highly accurate in predicting an aberration distribution that meets
      the requirements through an inverse sensitivity analysis and can calculate the wavefront aberration margin based
     on imaging indicators.  © 2023 Optica Publishing Group

1. INTRODUCTION

From the technology node of 5 nm and beyond, the technology
of extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) with a 13.5 nm
wavelength, as shown in Fig. 1, has been utilized in the expo-
sure process of the critical layer [1,2]. The dramatic reduction
in the wavelength and numerical aperture (NA) has obvious
advantages for the resolution and depth of focus. However, the
reduction of the wavelength also causes many optical effects
that were practically insigniﬁcant in traditional deep ultra-
violet lithography (DUVL) tools. A signiﬁcant factor in the
degradation of lithographic image ﬁdelity is optical wavefront
aberration [3]. As lens aberration  is inversely proportional
to the wavelength, the aberration in EUVL is above 10 times
larger than that in DUVL under the condition of the same
wavefront error [4]. For example, a 1.5 nm root mean square
(RMS) wavefront error at a 193 nm wavelength corresponds

B. Algorithm Selection and Evaluation

The relationship between aberrations and imaging quality is
complex and cannot be simpliﬁed as independent variables.
The quality of lithography imaging is affected by a combination
of multiple Zernike terms. Due to this complexity, it is not
possible to deduce the required aberrations based on imaging
quality requirements using physical laws or equations. It is fea-
sible to model the numerical relationship between aberrations
and lithography performance metrics in a “reverse” manner,
allowing for accurate predictions of the required Zernike term
